sections.overview: Rachow's notho is a small annual killifish native to seasonal freshwater habitats in south-eastern Africa.
sections.identification: Males are strikingly coloured, with blue and orange-red bars and a patterned tail; females are much more subdued.
sections.habitat: It inhabits temporary freshwater pools and flooded depressions in south-eastern Africa, including the coastal lowlands around Beira.
sections.diet: Species-specific field data on natural diet are limited in the sources consulted, so no detailed prey list is given here.
sections.behavior: Adults complete their above-ground life in pools that fill during the rains and dry out seasonally.
sections.reproduction: Like other annual Nothobranchius, its eggs develop in the substrate and withstand the dry phase; hatching follows renewed inundation.
sections.ecology: Its annual life cycle is adapted to waters that disappear between rainy seasons, and the known range is centred on eastern Mozambique.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern from 2019; this category does not remove the fish's dependence on seasonal wetlands.
